By evening the air of the house had altered from reserve to expectation. Helena knew the difference because reserve stood still, whereas expectation hovered over every object and asked to be noticed. The lamp on her desk burned with a steadier character than any person in the room. She had promised herself composure, yet composure is most difficult to keep when one has rehearsed it in advance. Her cousin requested an interview with unusual civility, which was already a form of confession. He remained near the hearth and praised the weather, the dinner, and the comfort of the room with that abundant politeness by which frightened men attempt to purchase delay. Helena let him continue until his own caution exhausted him. Only then did she lift the folded petition from the tray beside her inkstand and ask whether he had come to claim it or to deny it.
